title: Integration vocabulary map (wave 0)
description: The scope map an integrations prior-art survey builds before any angle runs. Every verdict below is checked against meta.classification; a map recording none leaves all of them unfalsifiable.

revision.description: Bumped on every amendment of this map.

scope_ref.description: The scope document this map was built against.

classification.description: The capability-map classification this survey was dispatched with, transcribed. REQUIRED and non-empty: every angle_applicability verdict is checked against it, and a map recording none leaves all of them unfalsifiable.

type.description: One of six axes, each with a declared SOURCE. The table naming each axis's input is in references/integration-vocabulary-map-guide.md; an axis whose input is undeclared has no bootstrap.

canonical.description: The one spelling this group is keyed on.

expansions.description: The other spellings the corpus uses for this canonical.

expansion_cap.description: Bounds the query TERMS inside this group. It does NOT bound the cell count -- the cell is keyed (group_id, source_id), so nothing here caps the number of groups.

negative_terms.description: Required on category and domain-noun groups, where the words are ordinary English and the false-positive corpus is large.

borrowed_from.description: The sibling survey this group's vocabulary was borrowed from, when it was not built here.

note.description: What the three wave-0 requests returned. A recorded zero here is a finding about the corpus, not a failure -- which is why a probe with no note is refused.

item.description: A term, or an uncovered CAPABILITY -- the capability-coverage record lands here.

absent_types.description: An axis with no group, with its reason in excluded[]. `pattern` is a standing candidate here: it is reachable only through the conditional b2.

owner.description: The one group that owns this term, so it is queried once.

angle_applicability.description: A verdict for EVERY angle the REGISTRY declares, in both directions. The count and the id set are NOT pinned here: the registry is the authority on which angles exist, and two statements of one set drift with only one of them running. `angle-verdict-complete`, `angle-verdict-unique` and `applicability-angle-unknown` own it, resolving against the registry.

holds.description: An always-on angle (a1, a2, a3) can never be false.

reason.description: A holds:false names the DECIDING value from the classification.

sources.description: Every registry row in exactly one of the two.

as_of.description: When THIS run observed the row.

access_status.description: What THIS run observed, where it probed. A row belonging only to angles this dispatch did not run is transcribed from the registry and carries `sanitization.status: not-fetched`, which is the field that distinguishes probed from unprobed. `blocked` is a REGISTRY-only value: a source that refuses this run belongs in skipped[] with cause_class refused, and allowing `active` plus `blocked` would make the contradiction unrefusable by construction. Where the registry and the map disagree, the map is the true one.

cause.description: Required wherever status is not clean.

cause_class.description: `refused` carries OBSERVABLE evidence -- an HTTP status, a redirect target, a challenge body, an auth wall. `no-holding-angle` means every angle carrying it records holds:false. A source a HOLDING angle carries stays ACTIVE even where the scope makes it unlikely to yield.
